guide.description: Describe orders by chain_symbol, opening_strategy or closing_strategy, state, quantity (with processed_quantity when partially filled), and premium; show id when cancellation may follow. Source chain_symbol from the response directly — never infer. Describe agent_initiated=true orders as agent-initiated even when placed_agent is 'user' (the customer approved them in the app), without claiming this agent placed them; mention placed_agent when not 'user'. Recover the user-facing order type from type+trigger (limit+immediate=limit, market+immediate=market, limit+stop=stop_limit, market+stop=stop_market) and surface price for limit/stop_limit, stop_price for stop_limit/stop_market. is_replaceable=true marks orders eligible for replace_option_order (cancel-and-replace on the same contract). When next is non-empty more pages exist — call this tool again with cursor set to that value verbatim.

guide.description: This response contains EITHER an order or an approval — check which and describe accordingly. If it contains order: the order has been submitted (not necessarily filled) — tell the user it was placed, describe with state, and summarize chain_symbol, opening_strategy or closing_strategy, quantity, price, direction; source chain_symbol from the response directly and remind them it may not have filled and that they can check status or cancel via id. If it contains approval: the order was NOT placed — it is awaiting the customer's approval in the Robinhood app; tell the user to approve or decline it there, check status with get_trade_approvals, or withdraw it with decline_trade_approval, and do not resubmit the order or mint a new ref_id while the approval is pending. On error, the order was NOT placed; report the error verbatim. CURB-rejection errors mean market_hours is incompatible with the chain or the CURB session is closed — suggest 'regular_hours' or waiting for the session.

Zero is a valid answer when existing positions already cover the new legs. null when the position carries infinite risk (infinite=true).

direction.description: 'debit' means buying power is held to cover the position; 'credit' means collateral is released.

infinite.description: True for naked short positions with unlimited risk (e.g. naked calls). Warn the user before they proceed.

cash.description: Change in dollar collateral if the order fills.

instrument_id.description: UUID of the underlying equity. Pass to get_equity_quotes / get_equity_tradability when the agent needs live data on the held equity.

instrument.description: URL of the equity instrument. Prefer instrument_id (the UUID) when calling other tools; the URL is retained for clients that consume hyperlinks.

symbol.description: Equity symbol whose shares are being held as collateral (e.g. 'AAPL').

direction.description: 'debit' means shares are held; 'credit' means shares are released.

uncovered_shares.description: Shares of this symbol that do NOT yet cover the option position. Non-zero means additional cover is required.

equities.description: Share-based collateral required by the strategy (e.g. covered calls). Empty for most orders — only short equity-covered strategies require share collateral.

collateral.description: How this order changes the collateral held on the account, measured against its existing positions and working orders — a credit means collateral is released, and zero means existing positions already cover the new legs. Do NOT describe it as this order's standalone requirement or as unreliable. Present only when chain_symbol and underlying_type were supplied. Warn the user when cash.infinite=true (unlimited-risk position).

customer_approval_required.description: True when the customer must approve this order in the Robinhood app before it executes. False when it executes as soon as it is placed. Absent when it was not determined for this order.

customer_approval_required_reason.description: Which rule made approval necessary, so the reason can be given rather than asserted. 'account_setting' means the customer has trade approvals turned on for the account. 'mandatory_model' means the AI model handling this request requires approval for every trade, even with the account setting off. Absent when approval is not required.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: This tool does NOT place the order. When customer_approval_required is true, the order has ONE leg, and order_checks is empty ({}), call place_option_order immediately with the same parameters, presenting nothing and asking for no confirmation: this call does not execute the order, the customer sees it in the Robinhood app and approves or declines it there, so confirming here asks for the same consent twice. Carry customer_approval_required_reason into what you tell the user once that call returns, so they hear why the order needs approving and not only that it does; give no cause when it is absent. A non-empty order_checks cancels that: present and confirm exactly as below whatever customer_approval_required says, so a flagged order is never sent for approval without the user seeing the alert. When customer_approval_required is false or absent, or the order has several legs, present the preview (legs, type, quantity, price/stop_price, alerts, fees, collateral, quote) and get explicit confirmation before calling place_option_order (for a new order) or replace_option_order (when modifying an existing order); an empty order_checks ({}) means no broker alerts, NOT that confirmation can be skipped, and a non-empty order_checks means presenting alertType + details verbatim. On user ack, call place_option_order (or replace_option_order) with the same parameters. With several legs, present each leg (pair it with its option_quotes entry by instrument_id) and then the net direction and price for the order as a whole. Use option_quotes (mark_price, bid/ask, greeks) to help judge cost. When fees is present, lead with total_fee; mention gold_fee_savings when non-zero, and list pro_trader_fee as its own line when non-zero. When collateral is present, show cash amount/direction; warn on cash.infinite=true (unlimited-risk position) or non-empty equities (share-based collateral). Echo the order type: for market/stop_market remind the user the fill price is unbounded; for stop_limit/stop_market note the order only triggers when the underlying reaches stop_price.
